# contexts/

## Purpose
The React providers `_app.tsx` wraps every page in: who the user is (`AuthContext`), which tenant they are looking at (`CompanyContext`), and two presentation preferences (`ThemeContext`, `ThemeModeContext`, `TableDensityContext`). `companyModel.ts` holds the pure half of the company state — storage keys, parsing, mapping — so it can be tested without React.

## Caller contract
`_app.tsx` mounts all of them. `AuthProvider` and `CompanyProvider` both take `skipFetch`, which `_app.tsx` sets during a PDF print render: `AuthProvider`'s `/api/auth/me` fails JWT verification on a print token and CLEARS the cookie carrying it, and `CompanyProvider`'s `/api/accounting/companies` 401s into `apiFetch`'s redirect to `/login`. See `src/lib/pdf/.claude.md`.

## Main signatures
- `useAuth(): { user, isAuthenticated, loading, logout }`
- `useCompany(): { activeCompany, companies, loading, companyRole, switchCompany }`
- `readStoredCompany()` · `readStoredCompanyId(onParseError?)` · `writeStoredCompany(entry)` · `clearStoredCompany()` · `COMPANY_STORAGE_KEY` (`companyModel.ts`)

## Business rules
- **The server reads the `active_company_id` COOKIE, not anything this provider holds.** `withAuth` scopes every query by that cookie. `localStorage` (`isaflow_active_company`) exists only so the first client render has a name to show instead of flashing the fallback title. Only `switchCompany` moves the cookie: it POSTs `/api/auth/switch-company`, mirrors the choice into `localStorage`, then hard-reloads; on mount the provider follows the cookie (below).
- A changed user identity inside one provider instance drops the previous user's tenant state immediately, rather than leaving it visible until the refetch returns.
- **An outage is not a sign-out (D9).** `AuthProvider` keeps the known user when `/api/auth/me` answers 5xx/408/429 or cannot be reached, keeps a FIRST check in `loading` (so `AdminLayout` does not redirect to `/login`) and retries every `AUTH_RETRY_AFTER_SECS`. It exposes `authUnavailable`, so `AppLayout`'s pending screen (`src/components/layout/AuthPendingScreen.tsx`) says the sign-in service is unreachable and the user is still signed in, with a Retry button; the page appears by itself when `/me` answers. Only another non-OK status (401/403) clears the user. Tests: `tests/unit/components/authOutageClient.test.tsx`, `authUnavailableScreen.test.tsx`.
- Memberships are always fetched, super admins included. A previous short-circuit that trusted `localStorage` for super admins left the switcher empty and could pin the UI to a company the user could not leave.

## Business rule — the label names the company the SERVER serves (R-148)
`loadUserCompanies` activates the company in `activeCompanyId` from `GET /api/accounting/companies?action=user-companies` — the `active_company_id` cookie `withAuth` scoped that request to, membership-checked. `localStorage` is never a selection input: when it names another company it is cleared (and rewritten from the server's company once its details load), and the first-paint stub is dropped so a failed details fetch cannot leave the wrong name on screen. When the user-companies fetch fails or throws, no company is shown and `localStorage` is left untouched (a blip must not wipe a stored, e.g. impersonated, company); only a successful answer clears it. Nothing on mount POSTs `switch-company`, so a stale `localStorage` cannot move the session. Impersonation needs no branch: `impersonate-exchange` sets the cookie. Tests: `tests/unit/components/contexts/CompanySwitcherSessionCompany.dom.test.tsx`.

**Residual:** the check runs once per mount. A tab left open while another tab (or another app on the same cookie domain, e.g. a second dev port on `localhost`) switches company keeps its old label until it reloads, while its API calls follow the new cookie.

- `tests/unit/components/contexts/` — provider behaviour, including the print-render gate.
